name: Dola
oneLiner: DOLA is Inverse Finance's CDP-style stablecoin minted against overcollateralized loans in the FiRM lending protocol, with USDS as a peg backstop.
collateral: Over-collateralized assets deposited in Inverse Finance's FiRM fixed-rate lending markets, currently dominated by DOLA paired stablecoin collateral markets; USDS in the PSM remains a peg backstop
pegMechanism: DOLA is minted through Inverse Finance FiRM Fed and PSM Fed facilities, with legacy Frontier Fed liquidity winding down. Supply expands or contracts through governed lending-market and PSM rails rather than the old DEX Liquidity Fed model.

oracleRisk.summary: Inverse FiRM values isolated collateral markets through Pessimistic Price Oracles that choose the conservative value across a primary and fallback path before applying market-specific collateral and liquidation parameters.

branchApplicability.reviewer: Codex Safety Score V9 data research
branchApplicability.rationale: DOLA is borrowed from isolated FiRM markets whose collateral types have separately governed collateral factors, liquidation factors, incentives, borrow caps, and oracle configurations. The markets share the documented Pessimistic Price Oracle and FiRM liquidation architecture, so they are represented as one common mechanism branch rather than unsupported per-market parameter estimates.

oracleRisk.reviewer: Codex Safety Score V9 data research

branches.label: FiRM isolated collateral markets
branches.summary: Governance-approved FiRM markets share conservative dual-path price selection, isolated collateral escrows, and third-party liquidation against market-specific risk parameters.

feeds.path: Primary price source and fallback/TWAP path -> conservative lower collateral price -> FiRM market

branches.fallbackBehavior: FiRM's Pessimistic Price Oracle compares independent price paths and uses the lower collateral value; current documentation describes Chainlink plus a fallback or time-weighted path, with governance able to update oracle configuration.

collateralParameters.note: Each isolated market has governance-set collateral factor, liquidation factor, liquidation incentive, supply ceiling, and daily borrow limits; values differ by collateral and are not collapsed into one estimate.

branches.liquidationMechanism: When a loan breaches its market collateral factor, third-party liquidators repay DOLA debt and receive collateral plus the market liquidation incentive; depleted DBR can first trigger repeated permissionless replenishment that adds DOLA debt until liquidation eligibility is reached.
branches.backstop: For governance-approved FiRM markets, jrDOLA is a voluntary first-loss DOLA vault whose assets can be slashed to repay liquidation shortfalls; uncovered losses outside that coverage remain a claim on protocol reserves.
branches.shutdownOrBadDebtBehavior: FiRM isolates collateral markets so a market shortfall does not directly pool collateral risk across borrowers. Selected bad debt can slash jrDOLA before protocol reserves; reviewed documentation does not describe a global DOLA shutdown or holder settlement path.

mintAuthority.summary: DOLA minting is controlled by the token operator, a Compound Timelock (48h delay) administered by a Compound GovernorBravo using INV governance token. All DOLA supply changes require an on-chain INV vote followed by a 48-hour timelock execution delay.

mintIncidents.summary: Inverse Finance's Anchor/Frontier oracle-manipulation incident let an attacker borrow and withdraw DOLA against manipulated collateral, leaving bad debt through the stablecoin issuance route.

controls.label: DOLA token operator (Timelock, 48h delay)
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25294782: DOLA.operator() = 0x926dF14a23BE491164dCF93f4c468A50ef659D5B confirmed. Contract bytecode identified as Compound Timelock: admin() = 0xbeccb6bb0aa4ab551966a7e4b97cec74bb359bf6 (GovernorBravo), delay = 0x2a300 = 172800s (48h). GovernorBravo slot 0 stores Timelock address confirming circular DAO governance pairing.

review.evidence: At Ethereum block 25294782: DOLA operator() confirmed = Timelock 0x926dF14a (48h delay). Timelock admin = 0xbeccb6bb (GovernorBravo, INV-token governance). GovernorBravo slot 0 = Timelock address (standard Compound Bravo pairing). Full DAO governance chain confirmed: INV vote → GovernorBravo → 48h Timelock → DOLA mint/burn. No multisig bypass. DOLA minting is over-collateralised issuance controlled by the token operator, which at block 25294782 is a Compound Timelock with a 48-hour delay administered by INV-token GovernorBravo; every supply change requires an on-chain INV vote followed by the independently enforced 48-hour execution delay, so the encoding-derived direct-mint cap is economically raiseable rather than unbounded and DOLA falls outside the fiat-custodial centralized-mint scope.

notices.title: Historical oracle-manipulation incident
notices.message: Inverse Finance suffered an April 2022 oracle-manipulation exploit that let an attacker borrow and withdraw DOLA against manipulated collateral, leaving bad debt through the stablecoin issuance route.

reserves.name: Governance tokens (INV, CRV, CVX)
reserves.issuerOrObligor: Inverse Finance (INV), Curve (CRV), and Convex (CVX) governance tokens

reserveReview.reviewer: Kimi P2 reserve cohort rc-7 (lead tusd-trueusd)
reserveReview.rationale: The FiRM markets API fetched on 2026-07-20 reported $42,982,738 of total DOLA debt; bucketing each market's debt through the reviewed DOLA live-reserve adapter mapping yields sUSDe 81.0%, sUSDS 12.3%, the sDOLA-scrvUSD Curve LP 3.4%, ETH/LST 1.5%, governance tokens 1.3%, and BTC 0.5%, summing to 100.0% on the adapter's exact identities. Since the 2026-07-14 review the sDOLA-scrvUSD LP slice grew from 1.4% to 3.4% and sUSDe eased from 82.7% to 81.0%, so curated weights were re-aligned to the 2026-07-20 live rows and every slice now carries a complete classification. The scope is restated as full-composition: the six slices cover the entire observed FiRM collateral envelope. The remaining slices are not silently linked: the sDOLA-scrvUSD Curve LP needs a constituent split, while ETH/LST, governance-token, and BTC collateral are identified exogenous assets outside the stablecoin dependency graph.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Current DOLA debt outstanding by FiRM collateral market (API fetched 2026-07-20), aggregated with the reviewed DOLA live-reserve adapter
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: The 3.4% Other collateral slice is the sDOLA-scrvUSD Curve LP; its self and scrvUSD legs cannot be weighted from the aggregate market debt alone.

nonLinkDispositions.rationale: The slice contains ETH and liquid-staking collateral rather than a tracked stablecoin dependency.
The API identifies this debt as an sDOLA-scrvUSD Curve LP market but does not split the self and scrvUSD constituent weights.
Governance-token collateral is identified but is not a stablecoin dependency.
Bitcoin collateral is identified but is not a stablecoin dependency.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: DOLA cross-chain deployments are reviewed through Inverse Finance documentation that identifies Chainlink CCIP bridges and chain-specific Fed contracts. CCIP is an external validation and messaging route, so the bridge-route tier is external validated network rather than issuer-native settlement.

routes.reviewNote: Native DOLA on Ethereum: minting is controlled by the token operator, a Compound Timelock (48h delay) administered by INV-token GovernorBravo, per the verified mint-authority review (2026-07-16). No bridge mints this deployment.

Verified on Arbitrum 2026-07-20 (block 485690756): DOLA 0x6a7661795c374c0bfc635934efaddff3a7ee23b6 is a BeaconProxy to the shared StandardArbERC20 implementation 0x3f770Ac673856F105b586bb393d122721265aD46; l1Address() = 0x865377367054516e17014ccded1e7d814edc9ce4 (Ethereum DOLA) and l2Gateway() = 0x09e9222e96e7b4ae2a407b98d48e330053351eee (Arbitrum L2 ERC20 Gateway), which is the mint/burn authority for this canonical bridge representation.

Verified on Base 2026-07-20 (block 48862205): DOLA 0x4621b7a9c75199271f773ebd9a499dbd165c3191 reports bridge() and l2Bridge() = 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000010 (Base L2StandardBridge predeploy), the mint/burn authority for this canonical bridge representation of Ethereum DOLA.

Verified on Optimism 2026-07-20 (block 154457492): DOLA 0x8ae125e8653821e851f12a49f7765db9a9ce7384 reports l2Bridge() = 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000010 (Optimism L2StandardBridge predeploy), the mint/burn authority for this canonical bridge representation of Ethereum DOLA.

Verified on Fantom 2026-07-20 (block 122578711): DOLA 0x3129662808bec728a27ab6a6b9afd3cbaca8a43c (name 'Dola USD Stablecoin') owner() = 0xc564ee9f21ed8a2d8e7e76c085740d5e4c5fafbe, which holds no Fantom bytecode (EOA). Follow-up reads on 2026-07-20 (block 122587402, rpcapi.fantom.network) positively identify the deployment as an AnyswapV5/V6-family Multichain anyToken rather than an unattributed legacy contract: vault() = 0xc564ee9f21ed8a2d8e7e76c085740d5e4c5fafbe (identical to owner()), isMinter(vault) = true, delay() = 172800 (48h), underlying() = 0x0 (no locally escrowed underlying, so the representation is mint/burn against source-chain escrow). That vault address is the same Multichain MPC EOA recorded on the unresolved Fantom DAI route in dai-makerdao.json, so the failure domain is the defunct Multichain MPC signer set, which has been non-operational since the July 2023 shutdown. The bridge-route model cannot honestly encode a bytecode-less MPC EOA as a contract controller (same convention as the unresolved Multichain rows in dai-makerdao.json), and no route-specific mint-controller contract exists. Left unresolved.

Verified on BSC 2026-07-20 (block 111009503): DOLA 0x2f29bc0ffaf9bff337b31cbe6cb5fb3bf12e5840 (name 'Dola USD Stablecoin', 18 decimals) owner() = 0xf7da4bc9b7a6bb3653221ae333a9d2a2c2d5bda7, a Safe multisig with getThreshold/getOwners = 3-of-6. The owner is the mint authority for this deployment; the signer set is not publicly attributed to a named entity in Inverse Finance documentation.
